records.issue_text: Substring match in _is_error_focused_query treats negated queries (!event.type:error) and malformed filters (event.type:error_level_2) as error-focused, causing wrong upsampled counts or Snuba column errors
records.rationale: In the new helper `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring check: `if "event.type:error" in query:`. This will incorrectly return True for negated filters like `!event.type:error` and for malformed/superset tokens like `event.type:error_level_2` because both contain the substring `event.type:error`. That can incorrectly enable upsampling via `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` for discover queries, leading to wrong counts or potential query issues depending on the selected dataset/columns.

records.issue_text: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only transforms the literal bare count(), leaving aliased (count() as foo) and compound aggregations (count_if, count(unique(...)), eps1m) un-upsampled, producing undercounted values
records.rationale: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py, transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites when column_lower == "count()". Any yAxis/column value like "count() as foo" or other count-based aggregations will not match and will be left untransformed, so eligible error queries would still use the un-upsampled count() semantics for those expressions, leading to inconsistent/undercounted results compared to the intended upsampling behavior. The added tests also only cover the bare "count()" case.
